label: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 7
knowledgePattern: Combine arithmetic terms with arithmetic logarithms
solution:
The first arithmetic progression gives x+z=2y, so x+y+z=3y=12 and y=4.

The logarithms also form an arithmetic progression. Their sum is therefore 3log2y. By the product rule, this sum is log2(xyz). Thus log2(xyz)=log2(y3) and xyz=y3=64. The answer is D.

hints.title: Use the middle term
hints.body: For three consecutive AP terms, the two outer terms add to twice the middle one. Apply that to x+y+z=12.
hints.recap: Three consecutive AP terms have sum three times their middle term.
hints.pitfall: The common difference does not need to be found.

recall.reminder: Three consecutive AP terms have sum three times their middle term.

hints.title: Add the three logarithms
hints.body: Apply the same AP sum fact to the three logarithms. Then combine their sum as the logarithm of a product.
hints.recap: The sum of logarithms of positive numbers is the logarithm of their product.
hints.pitfall: The requested product can be found without determining x and z separately.
hints.pause: Undo the logarithm to obtain the product.

recall.reminder: The sum of logarithms of positive numbers is the logarithm of their product.
